- [ ] End-to-end demo: add labor and bicycle items to POS cart, verify correct rendering, checkout succeeds

{"body":"## Problem Statement

The four core transaction modules — POS, Repairs, Orders, and Quotes — each implement their own customer selection logic, line item validation schemas, and UI components independently. This creates duplication (~150-200 lines of near-identical search/debounce/dropdown code per module), inconsistent behavior (customer required in some modules but optional in others), and makes cross-module changes error-prone because the same concept is implemented differently four times.

POS currently only supports parts-only line items, making it unable to serve as a reference implementation for the other three modules which already support labor and bicycle line types. The validation schemas are scattered across separate files with no shared variant definitions, meaning any change to how a "part" or "labor" line item works must be replicated manually in up to four different schema files.

## Solution

Make POS the clean reference implementation by:
1. Extracting the customer selector into a single shared component used by all four modules
2. Creating shared line item variant definitions that each module composes into its own validation schema
3. Upgrading POS to support all three line item types (part, labor, bicycle) matching the domain model already present in the database

## User Stories

1. As a cashier using POS, I want to select an existing customer or leave it blank for walk-in sales
2. As a cashier using POS, I want to add parts from catalog via barcode scan or search
3. As a cashier using POS, I want to create special (ad-hoc) products when item not in catalog
4. As a cashier using POS, I want to add labor services with hourly time tracking
5. As a cashier using POS, I want to add bicycle line items referencing templates
6. As a repair technician, I want optional customer on repair intake for walk-in repairs
7. As a repair technician, I want CRUD line items on repairs incrementally
8. As a salesperson, I want optional customer on orders for walk-in orders
9. As a salesperson, I want atomic parts/labor/bicycle line items when creating order
10. As a salesperson, I want optional customer on quotes for anonymous estimates
11. As a salesperson, I want CRUD line items on quotes incrementally
12. As a developer, I want shared CustomerSelector component used by all modules
13. As a developer, I want shared line item variant definitions in one file
14. As a shop owner, I want every part sold to reference catalog entry

## Implementation Decisions

### Module 1: Shared Customer Selector Component (Frontend)
- Extract from POS into `client/src/features/customers/components/CustomerSelector.tsx`
- Props: `{ customerId?: string | null, onSelect, required?: boolean }`
- All four modules import and use this component

### Module 2: Shared Line Item Variant Definitions (Shared Validations)
- Create `shared/validations/line-item-variants.ts` with part/labor/bicycle variants
- Each module composes its own discriminated union from shared variants

### Module 3: Customer Optional Across All Modules (Backend Schemas)
- Repairs: allow customerId null without existing/new customer path
- Orders: customerId changed to nullable optional
- POS/Quotes already optional — no change

### Module 4: POS Service Layer Upgrade (Backend)
- `createDirectSale()` handles labor and bicycle line items
- Stock validation only on part-type items

### Module 5: POS Cart Store Upgrade (Frontend)
- Cart supports discriminated union of all three line item types
- Cart display renders appropriate fields per type

## Testing Decisions

1. Shared Customer Selector — unit tests for selection callback, null handling
2. Line Item Variant Schemas — unit tests for each variant valid/invalid inputs
3. POS Sales Service — integration tests: parts-only, labor, bicycle, mixed-type cart
4. Orders Schema — unit test customerId optional

## Out of Scope

1. Line item UI components (parts/labor/bicycle sections) — deferred to later pass
2. Fixed-price labor services — hourly stays core
3. Bicycle inventory management — templates only
4. Inline customer creation at POS — walk-in only
5. Multi-payment split, invoicing, void auth guard","title":"[PRD] Cross-Module Generalization: Customer Component + Full POS Line Items"}

{"body":"## Parent

#242 ([PRD] Cross-Module Generalization: Customer Component + Full POS Line Items)

## What to build

Create `shared/validations/line-item-variants.ts` containing three reusable variant definition objects (part, labor, bicycle) that each module imports and composes into its own discriminated union schema. Refactor existing schemas (repair, quote, customer-order) to import from the shared variants file instead of duplicating base fields.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `shared/validations/line-item-variants.ts` created with three variant objects:
  - Part variant: `{ lineType: 'part', partId (required), description, quantity, unitPriceNet, vatRateId, discountPercent }`
  - Labor variant: `{ lineType: 'labor', laborServiceId (nullable), minutesWorked (nullable), hourlyRateSnapshot (nullable), description, quantity, unitPriceNet, vatRateId, discountPercent }`
  - Bicycle variant: `{ lineType: 'bicycle', bicycleId (nullable), bicycleBrand/Model/Year/Color/FrameSize (all nullable), description, quantity, unitPriceNet, vatRateId, discountPercent }`
- [ ] Existing schemas refactored to import from shared variants: `repair.ts`, `quote.ts`, `customer-order.ts`
- [ ] Unit tests for each variant: valid inputs pass, missing required fields fail with correct error messages, nullable fields accept null
- [ ] No behavior change — all existing validation tests still pass

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

<!-- AGENT-FINDINGS-START -->
## Agent Findings

### Archivist — 2026-06-01 (Round 1)

#### Semantic Conflict: Required vs Optional/Nullable Across Modules

The issue states `partId (required)` and `laborServiceId (nullable)` for the shared variants, but **existing module semantics differ**:

| Field | repair.ts | quote.ts | customer-order.ts |
|-------|-----------|----------|-------------------|
| `partId` | **required** (`z.string().min(1)`) | optional/nullable UUID | nullable/optional string |
| `laborServiceId` | **required** (`z.string().min(1)`) | optional/nullable UUID | nullable/optional string |

- **repair.ts** (line 200): `partId: z.string().min(1, 'partId is required')` — always required for parts
- **repair.ts** (line 207): `laborServiceId: z.string().min(1, 'laborServiceId is required')` — always required for labor
- **quote.ts** (line 63): `partId: z.string().uuid('...').optional().nullable()` — optional/nullable
- **quote.ts** (line 69): `laborServiceId: z.string().uuid('...').optional().nullable()` — optional/nullable

This means a single shared variant definition cannot enforce both semantics simultaneously. The builder needs to decide on one of these approaches:

1. **"Loose base" pattern**: Shared variants define all fields as optional/nullable, and each module tightens constraints via `.refine()` or schema composition (e.g., `sharedVariantSchema.extend({ partId: z.string().min(1) })`)
2. **Module-specific variant factories**: The shared file exports factory functions that accept a config object specifying requiredness per field
3. **Two tiers of variants**: A "strict" tier (repair semantics) and a "loose" tier (quote/order semantics), each composed from the same base

#### Existing Code Patterns — Both Files Already Use `baseLineItemFields` Spread

Both files already have near-identical `baseLineItemFields` objects using object spread into `z.object()`:

- **repair.ts** (line 189): `const baseLineItemFields = { description, quantity, unitPriceNet, vatRateId, discountPercent }`
- **quote.ts** (line 51): `const baseLineItemFields = { lineType, description, quantity, unitPriceNet, vatRateId, discountPercent }`

These are the natural extraction targets. Note that quote.ts includes `lineType` in the base while repair.ts puts it per-variant.

#### customer-order.ts Uses Flat Object (Not Discriminated Union)

**customer-order.ts** does NOT use a discriminated union — it uses a flat `z.object()` with all fields nullable/optional regardless of `lineType`. This is structurally different from repair.ts and quote.ts, meaning the shared variants file would need to support both composition patterns.

#### Test Coverage — Existing Tests Per Module

- **`shared/validations/__tests__/quote.test.ts`**: Comprehensive tests for create/update line items across all 3 types (part, labor, bicycle). ~250 lines covering valid inputs, missing required fields, boundary values.
- **`shared/validations/repair.test.ts`**: Tests intake schema extensively but does NOT test `createPartLineItemSchema` or `createLaborLineItemSchema`. Line item creation tests are absent.

#### Relevant Files Summary

| File | Purpose | Key Lines |
|------|---------|-----------|
| `shared/validations/repair.ts:189-215` | repair line item schemas (part + labor, discriminated union) | baseLineItemFields, createPartLineItemSchema, createLaborLineItemSchema |
| `shared/validations/quote.ts:51-83` | quote line item schemas (part + labor + bicycle, discriminated union) | baseLineItemFields, createQuoteLineItem*Schema |
| `shared/validations/customer-order.ts:4-20` | customer order line items (flat object, all nullable) | customerOrderLineItemSchema |
| `shared/types/repair.ts:86-115` | TypeScript interfaces for repair line items | RepairLineItem, CreatePartLineItemInput, CreateLaborLineItemInput |
| `shared/validations/__tests__/quote.test.ts` | Existing test patterns to follow | All 3 types tested |

---

### Archivist — 2026-06-01 (Round 2: Composition Approach Decision)

#### Resolution: Use "Loose Base" Pattern (Approach 1)

The PRD (#242) states: **"Each module composes its own discriminated union from shared variants."** This confirms the loose base pattern — the shared file exports plain field-definition objects, and each module spreads them into `z.object()` with module-specific overrides.

This is also the **established codebase convention**:
- `customer.ts` (line 17): `addressFields` object spread into both `createPrivateSchema` and `createCompanySchema`
- `repair.ts` (line 189): `baseLineItemFields` spread into part/labor schemas
- `quote.ts` (line 51): `baseLineItemFields` spread into all three variant schemas

#### Shared Variants File Structure (`shared/validations/line-item-variants.ts`)

The file should export **plain objects** (not Zod schemas) containing field definitions:

```typescript
// Base fields shared across ALL line item types
export const baseLineItemFields = {
  description: z.string().min(1, 'description is required').max(500),
  quantity: z.number().int().positive('quantity must be positive'),
  unitPriceNet: z.number().int().nonnegative('unitPriceNet must be non-negative'),
  vatRateId: z.string().min(1, 'vatRateId is required'),
  discountPercent: z.number().int().min(0).max(10000).nullable().optional(),
}

// Part variant fields (partId loose — module overrides for strictness)
export const partVariantFields = {
  lineType: z.literal('part'),
  partId: z.string().uuid('partId must be a valid UUID').optional().nullable(),
}

// Labor variant fields
export const laborVariantFields = {
  lineType: z.literal('labor'),
  laborServiceId: z.string().uuid('laborServiceId must be a valid UUID').optional().nullable(),
  minutesWorked: z.number().int().positive().nullable().optional(),
  hourlyRateSnapshot: z.number().int().nonnegative().nullable().optional(),
}

// Bicycle variant fields
export const bicycleVariantFields = {
  lineType: z.literal('bicycle'),
  bicycleId: z.string().uuid('bicycleId must be a valid UUID').optional().nullable(),
  bicycleBrand: z.string().max(100).optional().nullable(),
  bicycleModel: z.string().max(200).optional().nullable(),
  bicycleYear: z.number().int().min(1900).max(new Date().getFullYear() + 1).optional().nullable(),
  bicycleColor: z.string().max(50).optional().nullable(),
  bicycleFrameSize: z.string().max(20).optional().nullable(),
}
```

#### Module-Specific Composition Examples

**repair.ts** — tightens partId/laborServiceId to required:
```typescript
import { baseLineItemFields, partVariantFields, laborVariantFields } from './line-item-variants.js'

export const createPartLineItemSchema = z.object({
  ...baseLineItemFields,
  ...partVariantFields,
  // Override: tighten partId to required for repairs
  partId: z.string().min(1, 'partId is required'),
})
```

**quote.ts** — uses loose variants as-is (no override needed):
```typescript
import { baseLineItemFields, partVariantFields } from './line-item-variants.js'

export const createQuoteLineItemPartSchema = z.object({
  ...baseLineItemFields,
  ...partVariantFields,
})
```

**customer-order.ts** — uses flat object (no discriminated union), spreads all variant fields:
```typescript
import { baseLineItemFields } from './line-item-variants.js'

export const customerOrderLineItemSchema = z.object({
  lineType: z.enum(['part', 'labor', 'bicycle']),
  ...baseLineItemFields,
  partId: z.string().nullable().optional(),
  laborServiceId: z.string().nullable().optional(),
  // bicycle fields...
})
```

#### POS (sales.ts) — Needs Upgrade to Discriminated Union

Currently `cartLineItemSchema` in `shared/validations/sales.ts` only supports parts. The PRD requires upgrading POS to support all three line item types. After shared variants are created, sales.ts should be refactored similarly to repair.ts with strict partId:
```typescript
export const posPartLineItemSchema = z.object({
  ...baseLineItemFields,
  ...partVariantFields,
  partId: z.string().min(1, 'partId is required'), // POS requires catalog reference (PRD story #14)
})

export const createDirectSaleLineItemSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('lineType', [
  posPartLineItemSchema,
  posLaborLineItemSchema,
  posBicycleLineItemSchema,
])
```

#### Key Decision Summary

| Aspect | Decision | Rationale |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| Composition approach | **Loose base** (plain objects spread into `z.object()`) | Matches PRD language + existing codebase convention in customer.ts/repair.ts/quote.ts |
| Shared variant strictness | **All optional/nullable** for entity IDs | Allows each module to tighten as needed; loose base is the natural default |
| Module override mechanism | **Spread override** (`{ ...sharedFields, partId: z.string().min(1) }`) | Zod object spread naturally supports field override — last definition wins |
| customer-order.ts pattern | **Flat object** (no discriminated union) | Existing behavior preserved; shared base fields still extracted |

#### Files to Modify

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `shared/validations/line-item-variants.ts` | **CREATE** — new file with shared variant field objects |
| `shared/validations/repair.ts:189-215` | **REFACTOR** — import from line-item-variants, remove local baseLineItemFields |
| `shared/validations/quote.ts:51-83` | **REFACTOR** — import from line-item-variants, remove local baseLineItemFields |
| `shared/validations/customer-order.ts:4-20` | **REFACTOR** — import base fields from line-item-variants |
| `shared/validations/sales.ts:9-21` | **UPGRADE** — convert to discriminated union using shared variants (PRD Module 4) |

#### Test Strategy

- Create `shared/validations/__tests__/line-item-variants.test.ts` for the shared file
- Follow patterns from `quote.test.ts` (~250 lines, comprehensive coverage across all 3 types)
- Add line item creation tests to `repair.test.ts` (currently missing — gap identified in Round 1)
- Ensure existing tests still pass (no behavior change requirement)

<!-- AGENT-FINDINGS-END -->

{"body":"## Parent

#242 ([PRD] Cross-Module Generalization: Customer Component + Full POS Line Items)

## What to build

Upgrade `sale.service.ts` so that `createDirectSale()` handles all three line item types (part, labor, bicycle). Stock validation only applies to part-type items; labor and bicycle skip stock check. Pricing computation (`computeLineTotals`) applied uniformly across all types. **DB migration required**: `minutesWorked` and `hourlyRateSnapshot` are absent from `sale_line_items` (exist only on `repair_line_items`). Migration adds these two columns. `laborServiceId` and bicycle fields already exist via shared column spreads (`...lineItemColumns`, `...bicycleLineColumns`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] DB migration: add `minutes_worked INTEGER` and `hourly_rate_snapshot INTEGER` to `sale_line_items` table
- [ ] `server/src/db/schema.ts`: add `minutesWorked` + `hourlyRateSnapshot` columns to `saleLineItems` Drizzle definition
- [ ] `createDirectSale()` accepts discriminated union line items with `lineType` field (part/labor/bicycle)
- [ ] Stock validation only runs on part-type line items; labor and bicycle bypass stock check
- [ ] Pricing computation (`computeLineTotals`) applied uniformly across all three line item types
- [ ] Line item insertion into `sale_line_items` uses appropriate columns per type (partId for parts, laborServiceId/minutesWorked/hourlyRateSnapshot for labor, bicycle fields for bicycles)
- [ ] Integration tests: parts-only sale (existing behavior preserved), labor-only sale, bicycle-only sale, mixed-type cart
- [ ] Existing POS sales continue to work without change

## Blocked by

- #244 (Create Shared Line Item Variant Definitions)

## Out of Scope

The following are **explicitly NOT part of this issue** — they require separate slices/issues:

| Area | File(s) | Reason |
|------|---------|--------|
| Route handler | `server/src/routes/sales.ts` | Passes raw JSON to `createDirectSale()`; Zod validation in shared layer handles shape. No change needed unless response format changes (it doesn't). |
| Client-side types | `client/src/features/pos/types.ts`, `client/src/features/pos/store.ts` | Cart store and checkout payload are frontend concerns — separate slice under parent #242. |
| Client-side UI | `client/src/features/pos/components/*.tsx` | Labor/bicycle line item creation UI is a frontend feature, not a service-layer concern. |

<!-- AGENT-FINDINGS-START -->
## Agent Findings

### Archivist — 2026-06-01 (Round 3: Final Enrichment)

#### ✅ DB Schema Decision Confirmed: Option (A) — Add Columns via Migration

**PRD requirement:** User story #4 in parent issue #242 states *"As a cashier using POS, I want to add labor services with hourly time tracking."* This requires `minutesWorked` and `hourlyRateSnapshot` on `sale_line_items`.

| Column | On `sale_line_items`? | Action |
|--------|----------------------|--------|
| `laborServiceId` | ✅ Yes (via `...lineItemColumns`) | No change needed |
| `minutesWorked` | ❌ Missing — only on `repair_line_items` | **Add via migration** |
| `hourlyRateSnapshot` | ❌ Missing — only on `repair_line_items` | **Add via migration** |

**Migration file:** `drizzle/0002_add_labor_columns_to_sale_line_items.sql`
```sql
ALTER TABLE sale_line_items ADD COLUMN minutes_worked INTEGER;
ALTER TABLE sale_line_items ADD COLUMN hourly_rate_snapshot INTEGER;
```

**Schema.ts change** (`server/src/db/schema.ts`, line ~400): Add explicit columns to `saleLineItems`:
```typescript
minutesWorked: integer('minutes_worked', { mode: 'number' }),
hourlyRateSnapshot: integer('hourly_rate_snapshot', { mode: 'number' }),
```

#### 📋 Complete File Change List for Builder

| # | File | Layer | Change Required |
|---|------|-------|-----------------|
| 1 | `drizzle/0002_add_labor_columns_to_sale_line_items.sql` | Migration | **New file** — ALTER TABLE adding `minutes_worked` + `hourly_rate_snapshot` |
| 2 | `server/src/db/schema.ts` | DB Schema | Add `minutesWorked` + `hourlyRateSnapshot` to `saleLineItems` table definition (line ~400) |
| 3 | `shared/validations/sales.ts` | Shared Validation | Replace parts-only `cartLineItemSchema` with discriminated union using variants from `line-item-variants.ts` |
| 4 | `server/src/services/sale.service.ts` | Service Layer | Discriminate by `lineType`; conditional stock check (skip for labor/bicycle); per-type INSERT columns; handle bicycle fields |
| 5 | `shared/validations/sales.test.ts` | Tests | Add tests for labor and bicycle variants in validation schema |
| 6 | `server/src/routes/__tests__/sales.test.ts` | Integration Tests | Add mixed-type cart scenarios (labor-only, bicycle-only, mixed) |

#### 📋 Pattern Reference: Repair Service Labor Handling

`server/src/services/repair.service.ts` (lines ~1091-1128) shows the pattern for inserting labor line items with `minutesWorked` and `hourlyRateSnapshot`. The INSERT SQL includes these as nullable parameters. Use this as reference for the sale service's per-type INSERT logic.

#### 📋 Current State of Key Files
